\section[(dialogue)]{The body, family and verbs — a first pass}

\label{lesson:BN-R65-first-pass-the-body-family-and-verbs}



\begin{quote}
Say the words for a flower and a leaf.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item a hand, hair, a tooth, the throat, the stomach
  \item a shoulder, blood, a knee, the tongue, the head
  \item an ear, a fever, a hospital, pain, hunger
  \item happy, a doctor, a father, a son; a boy, a daughter; a girl
  \item a grandfather, a grandmother, an uncle, an uncle, an aunt
  \item an aunt, a husband, a wife, a child, a person
  \item a woman, a neighbour, to hear, to sit, to walk
  \item to play, to buy, to sell, to put, to open
  \item to wash, to laugh, to cry, to sing, to dance
  \item to learn, to forget, to want, to bring, to count
  \item to hold, to cut, to stop, to look for, to lose
  \item to wear, to leave, to throw, to fly, to teach
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
A hand? (\textbf{\bn{হাত}}, \emph{hāt}.) Hair? (\textbf{\bn{চুল}}, \emph{chul}.) A tooth? (\textbf{\bn{দাঁত}}, \emph{dā̃t}.) The throat? (\textbf{\bn{গলা}}, \emph{gôlā}.) The stomach? (\textbf{\bn{পেট}}, \emph{peṭ}.) A shoulder? (\textbf{\bn{কাঁধ}}, \emph{kā̃dh}.) Blood? (\textbf{\bn{রক্ত}}, \emph{rôkto}.) A knee? (\textbf{\bn{হাঁটু}}, \emph{hā̃ṭu}.) The tongue? (\textbf{\bn{জিভ}}, \emph{jibh}.) The head? (\textbf{\bn{মাথা}}, \emph{māthā}.) An ear? (\textbf{\bn{কান}}, \emph{kān}.) A fever? (\textbf{\bn{জ্বর}}, \emph{jbôr}.) A hospital? (\textbf{\bn{হাসপাতাল}}, \emph{hāspātāl}.) Pain? (\textbf{\bn{ব্যথা}}, \emph{bæthā}.) Hunger? (\textbf{\bn{খিদে}}, \emph{khide}.) Happy? (\textbf{\bn{খুশি}}, \emph{khushi}.) A doctor? (\textbf{\bn{ডাক্তার}}, \emph{ḍāktār}.) A father? (\textbf{\bn{বাবা}}, \emph{bābā}.) A son; a boy? (\textbf{\bn{ছেলে}}, \emph{chhele}.) A daughter; a girl? (\textbf{\bn{মেয়ে}}, \emph{meye}.) A grandfather? (\textbf{\bn{দাদু}}, \emph{dādu}.) A grandmother? (\textbf{\bn{দিদিমা}}, \emph{didimā}.) An uncle? (\textbf{\bn{কাকা}}, \emph{kākā}.) An uncle? (\textbf{\bn{মামা}}, \emph{māmā}.) An aunt? (\textbf{\bn{মাসি}}, \emph{māshi}.) An aunt? (\textbf{\bn{পিসি}}, \emph{pishi}.) A husband? (\textbf{\bn{স্বামী}}, \emph{shbāmi}.) A wife? (\textbf{\bn{স্ত্রী}}, \emph{stri}.) A child? (\textbf{\bn{শিশু}}, \emph{shishu}.) A person? (\textbf{\bn{লোক}}, \emph{lok}.) A woman? (\textbf{\bn{মহিলা}}, \emph{môhilā}.) A neighbour? (\textbf{\bn{প্রতিবেশী}}, \emph{prôtibeshi}.) To hear? (\textbf{\bn{শোনা}}, \emph{shonā}.) To sit? (\textbf{\bn{বসা}}, \emph{bôsā}.) To walk? (\textbf{\bn{হাঁটা}}, \emph{hā̃ṭā}.) To play? (\textbf{\bn{খেলা}}, \emph{khælā}.) To buy? (\textbf{\bn{কেনা}}, \emph{kenā}.) To sell? (\textbf{\bn{বেচা}}, \emph{bechā}.) To put? (\textbf{\bn{রাখা}}, \emph{rākhā}.) To open? (\textbf{\bn{খোলা}}, \emph{kholā}.) To wash? (\textbf{\bn{ধোয়া}}, \emph{dhoyā}.) To laugh? (\textbf{\bn{হাসা}}, \emph{hāsā}.) To cry? (\textbf{\bn{কাঁদা}}, \emph{kā̃dā}.) To sing? (\textbf{\bn{গাওয়া}}, \emph{gāowā}.) To dance? (\textbf{\bn{নাচা}}, \emph{nāchā}.) To learn? (\textbf{\bn{শেখা}}, \emph{shekhā}.) To forget? (\textbf{\bn{ভোলা}}, \emph{bholā}.) To want? (\textbf{\bn{চাওয়া}}, \emph{chāowā}.) To bring? (\textbf{\bn{আনা}}, \emph{ānā}.) To count? (\textbf{\bn{গোনা}}, \emph{gonā}.) To hold? (\textbf{\bn{ধরা}}, \emph{dhôrā}.) To cut? (\textbf{\bn{কাটা}}, \emph{kāṭā}.) To stop? (\textbf{\bn{থামা}}, \emph{thāmā}.) To look for? (\textbf{\bn{খোঁজা}}, \emph{khõjā}.) To lose? (\textbf{\bn{হারানো}}, \emph{hārāno}.) To wear? (\textbf{\bn{পরা}}, \emph{pôrā}.) To leave? (\textbf{\bn{ছাড়া}}, \emph{chhāṛā}.) To throw? (\textbf{\bn{ফেলা}}, \emph{phælā}.) To fly? (\textbf{\bn{ওড়া}}, \emph{oṛā}.) To teach? (\textbf{\bn{শেখানো}}, \emph{shekhāno}.)
